recent_posts.title: NervesConf 2024 Talks
recent_posts.summary: The full set of NervesConf 2024 talk videos has been published on YouTube. Topics covered include what's new with Nerves, the relationship between Nerves and Linux, building a thermostat from concept to production, using Nerves and Elixir for autonomous systems, secrets management, product development with Nerves, and practical challenges in maturing IoT systems.

recent_posts.title: How to Build Systems That Stay Online When Everything Spikes
recent_posts.summary: A talk from Erlang Solutions by Camjar Djoweini examining how systems behave under pressure during traffic spikes and critical moments. It covers how failures cascade across services and what engineering practices and architectural decisions help keep distributed systems stable and online under high concurrency.

recent_posts.title: NervesConf 2025 Talks
recent_posts.summary: A curated list of talks from NervesConf 2025, covering topics such as secure cloud connectivity with Nerves, real-world control systems, porting Yocto to Nerves, time management in embedded systems, and creative projects like an arcade game built with Nerves. Talks are available on the Nerves Project YouTube channel.

recent_posts.title: Elixir v1.20.0-rc.4 released
recent_posts.summary: Elixir v1.20.0-rc.4 has been released, requiring Erlang/OTP 27+ and compatible with OTP 29. Enhancements include a new :dbg_callback option for eval functions, Process.get_label/1, improved undefined function error reporting, and Mix dependency override support. Bug fixes address Integer.extended_gcd/2 negative GCD edge cases, struct recompilation regressions, type propagation in guards, URI.merge path handling, and several Mix compile and test issues including Windows argv limits and umbrella build locking.

recent_posts.title: Learning Resources / Other Resources
recent_posts.summary: HexReader is a free, open-source Android app that lets Elixir developers browse and download Hex.pm package documentation for offline reading. It mirrors content from hexdocs.pm locally, supports searching any Hex.pm package by name, and includes a one-tap download for the official Elixir language docs. Built with Material 3 design, it requires Android 8.0 or higher. The APK and source code are available on GitHub.

recent_posts.title: a reference for integrating llm_composer into a real Elixir application
recent_posts.summary: Livellm is a small open-source Phoenix LiveView chat app serving as a reference implementation for integrating llm_composer into an Elixir application. It demonstrates streaming LLM output into LiveView in real time, switching between multiple LLM providers via a unified API, handling reasoning output separately, tracking token usage and cost, and persisting chat state with SQLite. The project uses OTP patterns, PubSub for streaming updates, and background tasks for non-blocking requests, showcasing how Elixir and Phoenix naturally fit LLM-powered chat use cases.

recent_posts.title: Building platforms that handle traffic spikes and stay reliable under load
recent_posts.summary: A talk by Lee Sigauke focused on building reliable platforms for gaming, betting, and entertainment that can handle sudden traffic spikes. Covers why systems struggle under sudden demand and shares practical approaches to maintaining reliability and smooth scaling under high concurrency, with emphasis on distributed systems and observability.

recent_posts.title: Would you use a Blog section? (Where you can post blog posts directly on the forum)
recent_posts.summary: The Elixir Forum is considering adding a dedicated Blog section where members can write and publish blog posts directly on the forum, rather than just sharing links to external blogs. The proposal outlines guidelines for this section including prohibitions on AI-generated content, requirements for Markdown formatting and TLDRs, and content conduct rules. Members can later migrate their forum blog posts to their own personal blogs. A community poll is included to gauge interest.

recent_posts.title: Elixir v1.20.0-rc.2 released
recent_posts.summary: Elixir v1.20.0-rc.2 release candidate introduces significant compiler improvements: ~10% faster compilation, a new interpreted mode (up to 5x faster, scales with CPU cores), and cross-clause type inference that catches more bugs and dead code. Struct definition changes now trigger fewer recompilations. New additions include Integer.popcount/1, List.first!/1, List.last!/1, and a Software Bill of Materials guide. A potential breaking change makes map.foo() and mod.foo (without parens) raise errors instead of runtime warnings. Mix gains parallelized dep lock status checks and the interpreted module definition option.

recent_posts.title: Elixir Programming Language Forum
recent_posts.summary: The Elixir Forum celebrates its 10th anniversary with impressive milestones: nearly 10M emails sent, 100M pageviews served, and over $100K in prizes given away. The community has created 40K threads and posted 400K times. The forum announces upcoming structural changes to adapt to LLMs and evolving usage patterns, moving away from single-thread-per-library policies. Birthday celebrations include three new giveaways (Pragmatic Studio courses, AppSignal subscriptions, plus existing PragProg, Manning, and ElixirCasts prizes), expanded discounts from sponsors, and recognition of 50 Members of the Year. The post reflects on the forum's intentional design choices around SEO, community building, and quality content that differentiated it from typical programming forums.
